cells.title: Add the bee skillstation install and alias verbs
cells.action: Add a verb group `bee skillstation` in a new module verbs/skillstation_group.rs, wired into verbs/mod.rs the way tmp_group is (D1). Verbs: `install [--apply] [--json]` and `alias <id> [--force] [--json]`. One const table RELATED_SKILLS holds id, repo `https://github.com/cursor/plugins` and path `pstack/skills/<id>` for statechart, create-formal-verification-skill, maintain-formal-verification-skill (D2). Reuse onboard/apply.rs run_skillstation (make it pub(crate)). install: for each row run `skillstation skill show <id> --json`; state present-active, present-draft, missing or skipped(reason). With --apply: add each missing row via `skillstation skill add <repo> --path <path> --id <id> --yes` and print `skillstation skill review <id>` as the owner's next step (D3); write an alias for each active row whose SKILL.md frontmatter (the `content` field) has `disable-model-invocation: true` (D4). Without --apply nothing is written. alias <id>: `skill show <id> --json`; not active → non-zero exit naming why (D7); else write the alias. Alias = `.claude/skills/<id>/SKILL.md` only, frontmatter name, one-line description from manifest.description, `disable-model-invocation: true` only when the hub skill has it, `metadata:\n  skillstation_alias: <id>`; body of at most 6 lines telling the agent to call the skillstation MCP tool `skill_get` with skill_id `<id>` and follow the returned content as this skill, and to tell the user to run `skillstation connect -g` when the tool is missing (D5). Ownership: overwrite only a SKILL.md carrying `skillstation_alias: <id>`; any other existing `.claude/skills/<id>/` refuses naming the folder unless --force (D6). Missing binary, non-zero exit or bad JSON = one skip row with reason, exit 0 for install (D7). Claude Code only (D8). Add registry entries for both verbs in generated/registry_payload.json following command-surface.md so `bee skillstation install --help` prints its flags. Tests in the module: drive a fake `skillstation` shell script put first on PATH (cfg(unix)) for present/missing/skip/apply; pure tests for alias render and ownership refusal and --force.

truths: bee skillstation install without --apply writes nothing and lists every RELATED_SKILLS row
bee skillstation alias <id> for an active hub skill writes .claude/skills/<id>/SKILL.md containing skill_get and skillstation_alias: <id>
an existing non-alias .claude/skills/<id>/ is refused without --force
a missing skillstation binary gives skip rows and exit 0 for install

artifacts.substantive: install and alias verbs, RELATED_SKILLS, alias render, tests

prohibitions: Never approve hub content or run skill activate
Never write a hub file directly
open_choices: Text report layout, as long as each row names id, state and next step

cells.title: Document Skillstation in the README and the knowledge bundle
cells.action: Add a short `Skillstation` section to README.md: why hub skills cannot be started with /<id>, what `bee skillstation install [--apply]` and `bee skillstation alias <id> [--force]` do, and that content approval stays with the hub owner (`skillstation skill review <id>`). Write one knowledge concept under docs/knowledge/areas/onboarding/ for the verb group, citing history D-numbers as `skillstation-aliases D<n>` (never raw decision ids), with Pointers to skillstation_group.rs. Run `bee knowledge consolidate --feature skillstation-aliases`, write docs/history/skillstation-aliases/delivery.md listing each concept changed, one line each. Run `.bee/bin/bee knowledge check` green. One commit.

truths: README.md has a Skillstation section naming both commands
a docs/knowledge/areas/onboarding concept describes the verb group anchored to skillstation_group.rs
key_links: the delivery lands in the same merge as the code
prohibitions: No restating of code in concepts
